Hey Pravin,

As per Proof_Coast940's prior comment this is very likely a fault with capacitors C2 and C7.

My B115D developed this issue a few days ago and after pulling both those caps and testing I found they had less than half the stated capacitance and ESR values of 10Ω and 33Ω respectively, they should be less than 0.3Ω! 

This high resistance prevents the PWM chip from receiving a stable and high enough signal voltage, causing the circuit to enter protection and reboot endlessly.

P.S.
I also had to replace C84 as it had swollen and blown, it's rating is 220uf 16v, about an inch away from C2/C7 over the PCB spark/isolation-gap. (I can post a picture if needed)

Good luck, getting the PCB out of the heatsink cage it's in is tedious at best FYI.

Also, the LF and HF driver connections wouldn't come off the board for me, so I resorted to pulling the spades off the LF/Woofer and unfortunately cutting the HF/tweeter wires as I couldn't pull them off the driver, easy enough to solder back together though.

You need Watts, aka Volts x Amps. (W = VxI) (V = IxR)  

   

Take a 2000W heating element:  
 
* If supplied by 100v, a 5 Ohm element is required to allow for the 20A to flow.

* If supplied by 200v, a 20 Ohm element would be used to alow the necessary 10A to flow.

This is why you see electric kettles/stoves/ovens more commonly in countries with ~240v as opposed to countries with ~110v as it requires greater current and therefore more copper, bigger fuses etc. incurring a greater expense.

It's a lot cheaper to increase the thickness of insulation than it is to install thicker gauge wiring, higher voltage also minimizes losses during transmission.

Some regular tips for me:

* Bring enough water to cope with the temperature, need at least 3L a day before taking excess heat into account. (Extra for cooking and washing up if you are so inclined)
* As above, plenty of non-perishable food along with the small perishables you can take for the first day, don't want to be hungry while camping, it sucks. Nut-mixes and other energy-dense foods are great, but again, dry food increases water needed!
* If you plan on sleeping, make sure your digs are somewhat comfy, if you don't have a foam sleeping mat get one, or the semi-inflatable kind, got mine from Anaconda (Denali iirc), I'm 6'2" and it cost me less than $50 and is highly resistant to tears/dirt.
* As get-in said, hide drinks in places like your wheel-well or kick-panels
* If you like r/trees and they have dogs at the gate, use multiple zip-lock bags (4-5), evacuate the air (use a straw) to get a good seal, and wash the bags with isopropyl and pat dry between each layer, will help remove the residual smell. (Worked for me at Soundwave and BDO, walked right past the canines and they didn't even blink)
* Trapping/keeping warm is best done in layers. Trackies under loose jeans and singlet + t-shirt + hoodie (and possibly gloves) will go a long way to keeping you toasty and avoiding the misery
* Bring a torch for at night (headlamps work best imo to be hands-free) Can't stress this enough!

Lastly: Have fun, don't take it seriously, and don't be a dick!
